title: Execution commutes with pullback
statement:
Let $p$ be a finite-message deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be maps into those input types. Then for every pair of inputs $x' : X'$ and $y' : Y'$, executing the pullback protocol $p.\mathrm{comap}\,f_X\,f_Y$ on $(x', y')$ yields the same output as executing $p$ on the transported inputs $(f_X(x'), f_Y(y'))$; that is,
\[
\mathrm{run}\bigl(p.\mathrm{comap}\,f_X\,f_Y\bigr)(x', y') \;=\; \mathrm{run}(p)\bigl(f_X(x'),\, f_Y(y')\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: p is a finite-message protocol over X, Y, α
replaced:
For all $x' : X'$ and $y' : Y'$,
$(p.\mathrm{comap}\,f_X\,f_Y).\mathrm{run}\,x'\,y' = p.\mathrm{run}\,(f_X\,x')\,(f_Y\,y')$.
